canFinish: ^Oh? You collected the coins? Go give them to my friend over there and he'll give you a reward!

c-1: ^Oh? These coins are for me? Thank you!

b: ^Sorry—come back after you’ve wrapped up that coin thing.

npcSmallTalk_Menu: ^Why are there coins all over the floor?

c-0: ^Can't complain. Happy wife happy life y'know?
c-1: ^A couple of weirdos posted up over there trying to get people to collect coins for them.
c-2: ^I honestly don't know, but I wouldn't be complainin' if I were you!

npc_Random_Dialogue: ^Can you take me to the team fight area ?

c-0: ^Hangin' around, just enjoying the evening cool.
c-1: ^I don't know it's my first day out here!

npc_TRPG: ^Hey, you defeat all those enemies yet?

canStart: ^Your uncle Linus turned for the worse in the night. He is in Redwillow across the river.
^Luma can brew a Solara Bloom tonic for him, but only if you bring her the flower today. The bloom opens once, at noon, at the shrine. The gate there needs all four of you.
^After Luma brews it, your uncle needs to drink the tonic before sunset if you want its full strength.
^We move in a second. If we start this day by rushing past each other, it will only get worse once we are tired.
^She is right. If everybody starts talking at once, I lose the plot and follow the wrong thing.
^Then we name one rule for ourselves before we go. What's going to hold our group together when things start going wrong?
^Listen all the way through before answering.
^Clarify what we're doing before we move.
^Ask for help before somebody gets stranded alone.
^Call problems out without turning on each other.
alreadyLeft: ^Good luck out there. Linus is counting on you.

norm_listen: ^Then that's the promise. Nobody gets cut off just because we are in a hurry.
^Good. Then nobody gets skipped because someone louder is in a hurry.
^Fine. Just do not let listening turn into stalling.
norm_clarify: ^Then we slow down long enough to name the thing we're doing before we rush it.
^Good. If I know what the job is, I can stay with it. My side ideas are rarely an improvement.
^That keeps us from solving the wrong problem.
norm_help: ^Then we ask early, not after somebody is already in trouble.
^Ask fast, then. Not after somebody freezes up.
norm_respect: ^Then we say what is wrong without making the person next to us the enemy.
^Good. Hit the problem. Not the person.
Start_Lead: ^The east road to the shrine is open. Nobody expects another calm pause once you take it.
^Do we want one team leader? I can do it, but all of you will have to listen when things start going wrong.
^Or we can just work it out together as we go along.
lead_shared: ^We keep it shared unless we start tripping over each other. Aisha speaks up if she sees a risk. Joyce makes the call if we stall. Ralph, if you get lost, say it.
^Fine. If I call it, nobody waits.
^Good. Then everybody knows what each person needs to do.
^I can do that. Specific is good for me.
lead_joyce: ^You take point when the pressure spikes. Aisha speaks up if she sees a risk. Ralph, if you get lost, say it.
^Then I speak the second I see the wrong turn.
^That actually helps. Unsupervised Ralph has a poor record.

b: ^Joyce takes the front without another word. Aisha watches the edges. Ralph stays close enough to hear every call.
^Joyce still leans forward, but the group stays together around her. Aisha watches the edges. Ralph stays close enough to speak if he gets lost.

Start_Depart: ^Good luck! Linus is counting on you.

guard_push: ^Hey. You. The mayor's been waiting on you since dawn.
^We'll get there when we get there.
guard_push_b: ^Getting ready takes a minute. Leaving your uncle to die takes a day.
guard_what: ^Not my place to say. His place to say.
^Which is why you should be over there talking to him instead of over here talking to me.
guard_pushback: ^Your call. But the bloom only opens at noon and the mayor knows where the shrine is.
guard_during: ^Good. You're moving. That's what I like to see.
^Keep the square safe while we're gone.
guard_advice: ^Stay together. The road past the cart gets narrow and people make bad decisions when they're in a hurry.
^You look like people who might be in a hurry.
guard_doubt: ^You had that look people get right before things go sideways.
^Glad I was wrong. Now get moving — the road to Redwillow isn't going to walk itself.
guard_quiet: ^Get some rest. You look like you earned it. Go on, head out.

joyce_before: ^We're just standing here. I don't love standing here.
joyce_before_b: ^The right moment is the one where we stop talking and start moving.
^Talk to the mayor when you're done warming up.
joyce_ready: ^Have been since before you woke up.
^Talk to the mayor. The sooner we know what we're dealing with, the sooner we move.
joyce_during: ^We've got a job. Let's not forget that while we're chatting.
joyce_concern: ^One. We move as a unit or we don't move at all.
^I've seen groups fall apart at the first obstacle because everyone went their own direction.
joyce_after: ^We did what we came to do. Linus has a chance.

c-0: ^You could have. It would have just been uglier.
c-1: ^Same as always. Find the next thing that needs doing and do it.

aisha_before: ^I've been watching the square. Everyone's a little tense this morning.
aisha_tense: ^A little. But tense and ready aren't the same thing.
^I'd rather feel the weight of something before I carry it.
aisha_mayor: ^The letter mentioned Linus. Beyond that I didn't want to guess.
^Guessing before you have the facts tends to send you in the wrong direction.
aisha_during: ^We're in the middle of something. What do you need?
aisha_checkin: ^Checking in is good. Most people wait until something's already wrong.
^We're holding together. Keep it that way.
aisha_worry: ^A few. But worry without a plan is just noise.
^I'm watching. If I see something, I'll say it.
aisha_after: ^It's strange how much can happen in a single day.
aisha_alright: ^I think so. Tired. A little glad it's over.
^Ask me again tomorrow. I'll have had time to think about it properly.
aisha_calls: ^Most of them. The ones we got wrong taught us something too.

ralph_before: ^Oh good. Someone to talk to. I've been standing here trying to look purposeful.
ralph_purposeful: ^Probably not. Joyce keeps glancing over like she's already disappointed in me.
^Which, to be fair, is a reasonable baseline.
ralph_nervous: ^A bit, yeah. I do better when I know what the job is.
^Right now the job is just standing here, and somehow I'm still managing to do it wrong.
ralph_focused: ^Trying. My brain keeps offering me alternative ideas that nobody asked for.
^I've been saying no to them. It's going okay.
ralph_plan: ^A few, but they're the kind I can figure out by just watching what everyone else does.
^I find that works better than asking and then immediately forgetting the answer.
ralph_after: ^We made it. All of us. Including me, which I'll admit was not guaranteed.
ralph_came_through: ^Eventually. After a detour involving a rabbit.
^I'm choosing to remember the coming through part more than the rabbit part.
ralph_learned: ^Ask before you wander off. Stay where someone can see you.
^And rabbits are not, in fact, ever leading anywhere useful.

roadblock_intro: ^A cart has gone sideways across it, one wheel jammed in stone.
^Two locals are already blaming each other.
^If this load misses market, I lose the week.
^If you wrench that wheel free the wrong way, the bank gives out and we all lose more than a week.
^We can clear a lane and keep moving.
^Or we can spend one minute figuring out whose problem gets worse if we rush.

b: ^If someone has a better fast answer, now would be a good time.

roadblock_intro: ^What kind of team shows up here?
roadblock_resolve: ^Ask each of them what they need before anyone touches the cart.
^Let Joyce call the move before the argument gets worse.

roadblock_already_resolved: ^The lane is already clear. Keep moving.

roadblock_listen_first: ^One at a time. Quin, what do you need from us?
^The cart straight again. That is all.
^That bank cannot give way under us.
^Good. Now we have something we can use.
^Then that is the job. Straighten the cart without kicking the whole road loose.

b: ^Good. That is exactly why we said it.

roadblock_listen_first: ^Once everyone is talking about the same problem, the fix is simple.
^Joyce braces the cart. Quin and Liora guide the wheel clear. Aisha keeps everyone off the soft edge.
^Thank you for not making this uglier.
roadblock_listen_informed: ^We already know what both of you need. Quin, the cart straight. Liora, the bank intact.
^That is the job. Both at once.
^Then let us get on with it.
^That is the whole thing, right there.

b: ^That is exactly why we said it.

roadblock_listen_informed: ^Joyce braces the cart. Quin and Liora guide the wheel clear. Aisha keeps everyone off the soft edge.
^Thank you for not making this uglier.
roadblock_quick_call: ^Lift on three. Clear the wheel. Keep the stones where they are. We move in one pass.
^That gets us through. It does not make it a good answer.
^The lane opens quickly, but Quin and Liora are still glaring at each other when you step past.
^The cart is through. The argument is not.
^You cleared the cart, but the bank is rougher than I like.
^It will hold for now. I am coming back with tools tomorrow.

b: ^The wheel is clear. The road is open.

roadblock_wheel: ^The wheel is jammed in a gap between two flat stones.
^The axle is sound. The problem is position, not damage.
^A front lift angled toward the road center should let the wheel find its own way clear.
^The bank on the left edge has loose fill beneath the surface stone. It will not hold extra weight.
^File this away for when you are ready.

c-0: ^Lift from the front, angle toward center. Keep weight off the left edge.

roadblock_wheel_revisit: ^The wheel is still jammed in the stone gap. Front lift, angled center. Left edge stays clear.

b: ^The crate is already loaded back on the cart.

roadblock_crate: ^Grain sacks. Three have split open and are seeping into the road.
^There is a market seal on the largest crate. A date stamp from this morning.
^Quin was not wrong about the timing. This load is not going to wait.
^This explains why Quin is so tense.

c-0: ^Timed delivery. He does not have room to lose an hour.

roadblock_crate_revisit: ^Grain and a market seal. You already know what is at stake for Quin.
quin_roadblock: ^That wheel is jammed solid. Every minute it sits there I am losing trade.

quin_haul: ^Grain. Half a season's worth. If it does not reach market today, I sell it cheap tomorrow or rot it next week.
^Understood. We will keep that in mind.
quin_stuck: ^Wheel caught the edge stone on the downgrade. I tried to straighten it and the whole rig went sideways.
^Now Liora is in my ear about the bank like I do not already know what a bad bank looks like.
^She is not wrong to worry. But we will find a way through for both of you.

b: ^That was not as ugly as I expected.

liora_roadblock: ^Nobody is listening. This is exactly how banks give out.
^What is your concern with the bank?
^What would you do to free the cart safely?
^We hear you. Tell us what cannot happen.

liora_bank: ^The road edge here is loose stone over old fill. Too much weight in the wrong place and the whole side drops.
^Once that goes, there is no road for anyone for weeks.
^That matters. We will keep the weight where the ground is solid.
liora_safe: ^Lift from the front, not the side. Keep the stones in place. Let the wheel find the rut, do not force it.
^And keep everyone off the soft edge while you do it.
^Good. That is something we can work with.
liora_warning: ^Do not touch the bank stones. Do not let anyone stand on the soft edge. And do not let Quin rush it.
liora_roadblock_revisit: ^The bank is still too rough for my liking. Be careful.

b: ^Thank you for not making this uglier.
^You cleared the cart, but the bank is rougher than I like.
^It will hold for now. I am coming back with tools tomorrow.

joyce_roadblock_lead: ^Two people arguing is one person too many. Tell me what you need from me.
^What is your read on the situation?
^Wait for us to talk to Quin and Liora first.
joyce_roadblock_shared: ^We can clear a lane and keep moving. What are we waiting for?
^We want to understand the full problem first.
^What is your plan for the cart?
^Talk to the others before we decide.
joyce_read: ^One person needs a market delivery. The other is worried about the road edge. Those are not the same problem.
^The cart is the symptom. What they each need is what we have to fix.
joyce_clear_plan: ^Lift on three. Clear the wheel. Keep the stones where they are. One pass.
^I can call it the moment you are ready.
joyce_wait: ^Fine. But every minute they argue the job gets worse.

b: ^That took longer than I would have liked. But it held.
^Good. That is what moving looks like.

aisha_roadblock: ^Before anyone touches that cart, we should know what both of them actually need.
^What did you notice about the two of them?
^Do you think we can satisfy both?
^How do you want to handle this?

aisha_notice: ^Quin wants the cart straight. Liora wants the bank intact.
^Those are different problems with the same solution, if you are careful. But nobody has asked the right question yet.
aisha_both: ^Yes. If we name both needs out loud before we touch anything, we end up solving both at once.
^The mistake would be to only fix the one we heard first.
aisha_handle: ^Ask them each what they need. Not what they want from each other. What they actually need from us.
^Then we have something to work with.
